nodes.label: Collaborative consumption platforms

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_000
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: How do fashion rental platforms differ from traditional retail stores?
nodes.answer: Fashion rental platforms offer short-term access to garments through renting rather than selling them for ownership.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How has technology and increased digitization influenced the sharing economy in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Technology and increased digitization have led to the development of the platform economy, which facilitates Collaborative Fashion Consumption (CFC) by making idle capacities more accessible.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_002
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why are business models emerging in the sharing economy often described as 'disruptive'?
nodes.answer: The business models emerging as part of the sharing economy are often described as 'disruptive' because they change the way mainstream companies conduct their business, even though they remain rather niche.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_003
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do rental platforms remain niche within the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Rental platforms in the fashion industry are niche due to perceived risks associated with renting clothes, such as hygiene, health, and lack of ownership.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_004
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Does the rental platform founded in 2010 offer both subscription and per item options?
nodes.answer: Yes, the platform founded in 2010 offers both subscription and per item options.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_005
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the platform founded in 2017?
nodes.answer: Consumers can contribute by using durable, quality goods, intensifying use of goods, enabling repair, take back, and recycling, ensuring rental replaces product purchase, minimizing transport of goods, and reducing private vehicle kilometres travelled.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_006
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How can the concept of "no-ownership" impact the apparel industry?
nodes.answer: The concept of "no-ownership" in the apparel industry can have implications for apparel retailers, as it may shift consumer behaviour towards renting or borrowing clothes instead of purchasing them. This trend could potentially threaten traditional retailers who rely on sales of new clothing items.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_007
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: Why do platform entrepreneurs emphasize providing consumers the freedom to try different garments?
nodes.answer: Platform entrepreneurs emphasize providing consumers the freedom to try different garments without committing to purchasing them in order to reduce fast fashion consumption and offer a sustainable alternative to traditional fashion consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_008
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do platform entrepreneurs aim to intensify the use of garments through rentals?
nodes.answer: Platform entrepreneurs aim to intensify the use of garments through rentals by increasing the number of wears through the garments life cycle relative to when the garment is owned. They focus on dress rental platforms as dresses are garments that are rarely worn when owned.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_009
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do Battle et al. (2018) propose access-based consumption as a new business model for luxury and second-hand fashion businesses?
nodes.answer: Battle et al. (2018) propose access-based consumption as a new business model by emphasizing sharing and renting luxury fashion items instead of traditional ownership as a way to reduce waste and promote sustainability in the industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_010
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are the motivations for intended sharing economy participation according to Becker and Ellen (2017)?
nodes.answer: Becker and Ellen (2017) analysed motivations for intended sharing economy participation and found that motivations can be categorized into people, planet, or profit-oriented reasons.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_011
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are some potential implications for apparel retailers related to the "no-ownership" trend?
nodes.answer: The "no-ownership" trend in apparel could have implications for retailers, as it may lead to shifts in consumer behaviour towards renting or borrowing clothing instead of purchasing. Retailers may need to adapt their business models to accommodate this trend and offer rental or subscription-based services to stay competitive in the market.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How does the sharing economy concept tie into the development of fashion rental platforms?
nodes.answer: Fashion rental platforms are part of the sharing economy, which aims to maximize the use of idle capacities, such as garments, by sharing them through technological platforms.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_013
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What were some of the questions asked during the interviews regarding the business plans of the platforms?
nodes.answer: The interviews included questions about the business plans underpinning the platforms, such as their sustainability claims and practices. Additionally, the interviews delved into the purchase criteria for rental items and the demographics and motivations of platform consumers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_014
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What are the two most popular business models in the dress rental market?
nodes.answer: The two most popular business models in the dress rental market are short-term dress rental and subscription rental platforms.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_015
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: How do subscription rental platforms work in terms of membership and garment access?
nodes.answer: Subscription rental platforms operate on a tiered-membership service basis, where the cost of membership determines the number of garments that can be accessed in a month.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_017
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the goal of fashion rental platform entrepreneurs in terms of consumer behaviour?
nodes.answer: The goal of fashion rental platform entrepreneurs is to reduce fast fashion consumption by replacing product purchases with fashion rentals, giving consumers the freedom to access garments of their choice without committing to owning them.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_018
nodes.label: Factual
nodes.question: What do consumers care most about when it comes to fashion rental platforms according to one entrepreneur?
nodes.answer: According to one dress platform entrepreneur, consumers care most about the fit, quality, and uniqueness of the garment when it comes to fashion rental platforms. While designer labels are important in marketing, the focus remains on providing access to something unique and exclusive that others won't be wearing at the same event.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_019
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do platform entrepreneurs aim to intensify the use of garments through rentals, particularly for dress rental platforms?
nodes.answer: Platform entrepreneurs aim to intensify the use of garments through rentals by increasing the number of wears during the garment's life cycle compared to when it is owned. They emphasize that dresses are garments that are rarely worn when owned, making rentals a more sustainable option.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_022
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What are some alternatives to personal ownership in the fashion industry?
nodes.answer: Second-hand platforms and rental clothing schemes are examples of alternatives to personal ownership in the fashion industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_023
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How do rental schemes benefit from the ability to leave reviews/comments on peer-to-peer platforms?
nodes.answer: Rental schemes on peer-to-peer platforms can gain traction by offering the ability to leave reviews and comments, which serves as a trust-building mechanism for consumers to assess the quality and reliability of the rental service or product.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Circular economy initiatives|Collaborative consumption platforms_qna_024
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What could lead to the development of peer-to-peer rental schemes in the business-to-consumer rental industry?
nodes.answer: The comfort of consumers with renting and their preference for re-worn items in peer-to-peer transactions.
